content_html:
This income tax calculator estimates your 2026 federal return, the one you file in early 2027. It follows the same steps as Form 1040: add up your income, subtract adjustments to reach adjusted gross income, take the standard or itemized deduction, work out the tax, subtract credits and compare the result with what you have already paid. The bottom line is your estimated refund or the amount you would owe.

It looks at your whole year. To see how much of each paycheck you keep after withholding, Social Security and Medicare, use a take-home pay calculator instead.

How to use the calculator

  1. Filing status, wages and withholding: take wages from box 1 and federal tax withheld from box 2 of each Form W-2. Married couples filing jointly should add both spouses' figures together.
  2. Children and dependents: children under 17 at the end of 2026 can qualify for the $2,200 child tax credit; other dependents qualify for a $500 credit.
  3. Age and blindness: each box adds to your standard deduction, and being 65 or older also unlocks the new $6,000 senior deduction.
  4. Other income: interest, dividends, capital gains, self-employment profit, retirement income and Social Security. Capital losses can be entered as negative numbers.
  5. Adjustments and new deductions: IRA and HSA contributions, student loan interest, and the deductions for qualified tips, overtime and car loan interest that apply from 2025 to 2028.
  6. Itemized deductions: enter these only if they might add up to more than your standard deduction. The calculator picks whichever is larger.
  7. Credits and payments: estimated tax payments and any other credits you expect to claim.

2026 standard deduction and brackets

Filing statusStandard deduction10% bracket ends22% bracket starts
Single or married filing separately$16,100$12,400$50,401
Married filing jointly or surviving spouse$32,200$24,800$100,801
Head of household$24,150$17,700$67,451

Each rate applies only to the income inside its band, so moving into a higher bracket never reduces your take-home income. Qualified dividends and long-term capital gains are added on top of your other income and taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% instead.

Worked example

A single filer earns $75,000 in wages and had $8,000 of federal tax withheld during 2026.

  • Taxable income: $75,000 − $16,100 standard deduction = $58,900
  • Tax: 10% of $12,400 ($1,240) + 12% of $38,000 ($4,560) + 22% of $8,500 ($1,870) = $7,670
  • Refund: $8,000 withheld − $7,670 = $330

The effective rate is 10.2% of income, even though the top bracket reached is 22%. For a married couple earning $100,000 with two children, taxable income is $67,800 and the tax of $7,640 is reduced by $4,400 of child tax credit to $3,240.

What else the estimate includes

  • Self-employment tax: 15.3% on 92.35% of your net profit, with half of it deducted from income. A simplified qualified business income deduction of up to 20% of the profit is also applied.
  • Social Security benefits: up to 85% can be taxable, depending on your other income. The calculator applies the IRS worksheet.
  • Refundable credits: up to $1,700 per child of the child tax credit can be paid out even when you owe no tax, and the earned income credit is estimated from the 2026 tables.
  • High-income taxes: the 0.9% Additional Medicare tax and the 3.8% net investment income tax, plus the new limits on state and local tax deductions and on itemized deductions in the 37% bracket.

Limits of this estimate

The calculator does not cover the alternative minimum tax, capital loss carryovers, the wage and property limits on the business income deduction at higher incomes, or the detailed eligibility tests for each credit. The earned income credit is worked out with the formula rather than the IRS lookup table, so it can differ by a few dollars. Treat the result as a planning estimate and use tax software or a tax professional to file.

faq.question: When will I file my 2026 tax return?
faq.answer: Returns for the 2026 tax year are filed in early 2027. The usual deadline is April 15, 2027, and you can request an automatic extension to file, though any tax owed is still due by the April deadline.

faq.question: Why is my refund smaller than last year?
faq.answer: Common reasons include a raise or bonus that moved more income into a higher bracket, a change to your Form W-4 that reduced withholding, a child aging out of the child tax credit, or side income with no tax withheld.

faq.question: Should I itemize or take the standard deduction?
faq.answer: Take whichever is larger. Most households take the standard deduction, but people with a large mortgage, high state and local taxes, big medical bills or generous charitable giving may do better by itemizing. The calculator compares both automatically.

faq.question: How can I avoid owing tax next year?
faq.answer: Update your Form W-4 with your employer to increase withholding, or make quarterly estimated payments if you have self-employment or investment income. Paying at least as much as last year's total tax (110% if your AGI was over $150,000) generally avoids an underpayment penalty.

faq.question: Does this calculator include state income tax?
faq.answer: No. It estimates federal income tax only. State income tax rules vary widely, and several states have no income tax at all.

faq.question: Is my information stored or sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser, and nothing you enter is sent to a server or saved.
